# Welcome

This is the documentation for the React implementation of the Airbus Design System : [goto/design-system](http://goto.airbus.corp/design-system)

Other **official implementations**

- CSS: https://css.design-system.airbus.corp
- Angular (*restricted standard*): https://angular.design-system.airbus.corp

Find official and community resources in our [Awesome Design System](https://github.airbus.corp/Airbus/awesome-design-system) curated list.

## 👋 Newcomers

Please **submit a request to get onboarded** : [goto/design-system-onboarding](http://goto.airbus.corp/design-system-onboarding)

We will give you access to everything you need to get started.

For any question, feedback or issue [join our chatroom](https://mail.google.com/chat/u/0/#browse/chat/q=%22Airbus+Design+System%22&sorganization=outside&smembership=all)

## Installation

Install the latest version and save it in your `package.json` dependencies. (For NPM configuration see [our github readme](https://github.airbus.corp/Airbus/design-system#environment-setup))

```
npm install @airbus/components-react
```

To install a specific version or an alpha/beta/rc release

```sh
npm install @airbus/components-react@3.3.1 --save-exact # specific stable release
npm install @airbus/components-react@next --save-exact # latest alpha/beta/rc release
npm install @airbus/components-react@3.0.0-beta.1 --save-exact # specific alpha/beta/rc release
```

Please note that react >= 18 and react-dom >= 18 are peer dependencies.<br />

## Templates

If you're starting your project from scracth, we recommend the single page application template from the [devx platform](https://devx.airbus.corp/), which is based on [vite](https://vitejs.dev/) and includes the Design System as well as typescript support.

- https://devx.airbus.corp/create/templates/default/react-app
- See [Software Engineering guidelines for SPA applications](https://github.airbus.corp/pages/Airbus/software-engineering-guidelines-ssg/it_patterns/single_page_application/)

## Usage

Airbus Design System components are self-supporting, they will inject the styles they need to display. Therefore you don't have to import a global stylesheet.

Here is a quick example:

```js static
import React from "react";
import ReactDOM from "react-dom";
import { Button } from "@airbus/components-react";

function App() {
  return <Button variant="primary">Hello World</Button>;
}

ReactDOM.render(<App />, document.querySelector("#app"));
```

**Next steps**

- Refer to each component's documentation page to see how they can be used
- See <LinkTo kind="General/Visual Styles/Introduction" story="docs">Visual Styles Introduction</LinkTo> about global styles, themes and customisation

### Standard Font

Airbus Design System has been designed with the Inter font in mind, but this font is **not** included in the library.

To install the Inter font and save it in your `package.json` dependencies, run:

```shell
npm install @fontsource/inter
```

Then, you can import it within your app entry point

```js
import "@fontsource/inter/300.css";
import "@fontsource/inter/400.css";
import "@fontsource/inter/500.css";
import "@fontsource/inter/700.css";
```

Alternatively, you can load the Inter font from google CDN:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Inter:300,400,500,700&display=swap"
/>
```

### Monospace Font

If you need to use a monospace font, for example to convey system messages, setup Roboto Mono font.

```shell
npm install @fontsource/roboto-mono
```

```js
import "@fontsource/roboto-mono";
```

Alternatively, from google CDN:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto+Mono&display=swap"
/>
```

### Icons

We recommend using Airbus or Material Icons. See <LinkTo kind="General/Visual Styles/Icons" story="docs">Visual Styles/Icons</LinkTo>
